correctness.rationale: In Z/3, consecutive proper differences are ±1; abab is exactly an alternating triple of differences. An interior swap across difference b sends a,b,c to a+b,-b,b+c, nonzero precisely when a=b=c. The analogous endpoint test flips two equal signs. Endpoint runs of length 2 or 3 can be flipped in full, and length at least 4 leaves at least two unflipped signs after an endpoint flip. Interior runs of length 3 can be flipped in full and those of length at least 5 admit the first-three flip, leaving at least two signs. With singleton endpoint runs, a length-2 interior run has no candidate, and each length-4 candidate leaves a singleton between two opposite runs and produces abab. This covers one-run and shortest-length cases. Halving the even interior lengths gives ordered compositions into 1 and 2, with 3 initial symbols and 2 signs; the stated Fibonacci count and series follow. All lengths 3–17 matched a fresh direct literal-word and swap enumeration, not a substitute for the proof.
residual_risks: No claim of even-length connectivity, formal verification, or a result for arbitrary alphabet sizes or circular words.

value.rationale: The minimal duplicate-avoidance language and adjacent swap are independently natural. The all-length run criterion identifies exactly when local reconfiguration is impossible, including nontrivial new obstructions from forbidding abab. An exact isolated-state census and parity dichotomy are useful even without a connectivity theorem; the no-Hamiltonian observation alone would be weak since swaps also preserve content.
residual_risks: This does not determine nontrivial components or connectivity within a fixed content class.
